'''Lydie Koch-Miramond''' (1 June 1931 &ndash; 5 July 2023) was a French [[Astrophysics|astrophysicist]] and pioneer in the study of cosmic rays at the [[French Alternative Energies and Atomic Energy Commission]] (CEA). She played a major role in the development of French space astrophysics, especially in the discovery and study of galactic [[cosmic ray]]s.

== Biography ==
Lydie Berthe Miramond was born on 1 June 1931 in Paris. In 1954, she graduated from the [[ESPCI Paris|École supérieure de physique et de chimie industrielles de Paris]] (ESPCI), where she finished second in her class, the 69th cohort.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Les ingénieurs de la 69e promotion de l'ESPCI Paris |url=https://www.espci.org/fr/anciens/eleves/69/ |access-date=2026-02-06 |website=ESPCI Paris Alumni}}</ref> Computer scientist [[Alice Recoque]] was a classmate.<ref name=":0" />

She then joined the [[French Alternative Energies and Atomic Energy Commission]]'s (''Commissariat à l'énergie atomique et aux énergies alternatives'' ''-'' CEA) Physical Electronics Department, headed by {{ill|Jacques Labeyrie|fr}}. Whilst working there she collaborated with Italian physicist [[Giuseppe Occhialini|Beppo Occhialini]], a specialist in cosmic rays.<ref name="sf2a">[https://sf2a.eu/website2023/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/Lydie-Koch-VF2.pdf Nécrologie de Lydie Koch-Miramond] par la Société Française d'Astronomie et d'Astrophysique</ref>

In 1967, the CEA Physical Electronics Department was divided into two sections, with the establishment of a CEA Astrophysics Section in [[Saclay]], which Koch-Miramond headed until 1979. She continued work on cosmic-ray research, focusing on the investigation of heavy-nucleus isotopes.<ref name="sf2a" />

In addition to her scientific work, Koch-Mirmond was deeply engaged in the support of [[human rights]], especially in regard to China. She actively participated in [[Amnesty International]] until 2009 and contributed to publications on the responsibilities of scientists in connection with human rights and world conflicts.<ref name="sf2a" />

Lydie Koch-Miramond died on 5 July 2023 in [[Saint-Rémy-lès-Chevreuse]] at the age of 92.<ref name="sf2a" />

== Research ==
Throughout her career, she played a key role in the development of new detector technologies. This included instruments for studying cosmic rays, [[gamma ray]]s, [[X-ray astronomy|X-ray]] astronomy, Ge(Li) detectors for hard X-rays and Si(Li) detectors for soft X-rays, detection of [[Electron–positron annihilation|electron-positron annihilation]] lines and CCD detectors.<ref name="sf2a" />

Koch-Miramond played a key role in several [[High-altitude balloon|stratospheric flight]] programmes. The first led to the discovery of the first galactic electrons in 1963; another flight confirmed the observations in 1965. A further trans-Mediterranean flight led to the first measurement of [[positron]]s in galactic [[Cosmic ray|cosmic radiation]] in 1967.<ref name="sf2a" />[[File:High-altitude-balloon-1041.jpg|alt=Photographie couleurs d'un ballon de grande taille, dans lequel se reflète la terre bleutée et l'espace sombre|thumb|240x240px|High altitude balloon]]In 1975, under Koch-Miramond's leadership, two ISOFER balloon flights were carried out to measure the composition of cosmic radiation. In September 1975, one balloon travelled 2,000&nbsp;km at an altitude of 40&nbsp;km from [[Sioux Falls, South Dakota]] to [[New Jersey]]. These were precursors to the instruments installed on NASA's [[High Energy Astronomy Observatory 3|HEAO-3]]-C satellite, which launched in 1979. The instrument made it possible to study heavy nuclei in cosmic radiation using the geomagnetic field. Koch-Miramond later explained this in a video on the [[French Alternative Energies and Atomic Energy Commission|CEA]] website.<ref>{{Cite web |title=1975 : ISOFER, histoire d'un ballon |url=https://irfu.cea.fr/Phocea/Video/index.php?id=254 |access-date=2026-02-13 |website=L'Irfu, Institut de Recherche sur les lois Fondamentales de l'Univers |language=fr}}</ref> Koch-Miramond coordinated the development of the instrument with Bernard Peters of the Danish Space Institute, leading to the provision of the cosmic-ray nucleus spectrum which remained a benchmark for over 30 years.<ref name="sf2a" />

== Advocacy ==
She became a scientific advisor to the CEA's Directorate of Material Sciences and head of the ''Ethics in Science'' working group within [[EuroScience|Euroscience]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Koch-Miramond, Lydie (19..-....) |url=https://www.idref.fr/056754213 |access-date=2026-03-12 |website=IdRef}}</ref> She chaired the Human Rights and Ethics Committee of the [[Société Française de Physique]], following its creation in 1990.<ref>{{Cite journal |title=La recherche, un droit mondial |url=https://www.refletsdelaphysique.fr/articles/refdp/pdf/2020/04/refdp202067p46.pdf |journal=Reflets e la Physique |issue=67 |page=46}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Lydie Koch Miramond |date=July–August 2008 |title=La Commission des Droits de l'Homme et Questions éthiques de la SFP |url=https://www.refletsdelaphysique.fr/articles/refdp/pdf/2008/03/refdp_10.pdf |journal=Reflets de la Physique |issue=10 |page=4}}</ref>

Committed to [[human rights]], Koch-Miramond contributed to the book ''La Chine et les droits de l'homme'' (China and Human Rights) following a symposium on contemporary China organised by [[Amnesty International]] in 1990.<ref name="sf2a" /> In 2002, she signed an appeal in the newspaper ''[[Le Monde]]'' alongside 2,500 prominent figures ‘for a just and immediate peace in the Middle East’.<ref>{{Cite journal |date=13 March 2002 |title=appel pour une paix juste et immédiate au Proche-Orient |url=https://scholar.lib.vt.edu/InterNews/LeMonde/issues/2002/monde.20020313.pdf |journal=Le Monde |page=6}}</ref>

== Awards and recognition ==

* Chevalière of the [[Ordre des Palmes académiques]]
* Chevalière of the [[Ordre national du Mérite]] (17 June 1980)
* Chevalière of the [[Legion of Honour|Légion d'honneur]] (31 December 1991)
* 1989: Prix du CEA, shared with Jean-Jacques Engelmann and Philippe Goret, for research on the composition of cosmic rays and space detection techniques<ref>{{Cite book |url=http://archive.org/details/LeMondeDiplomatique1990FranceFrench |title=Le Monde Diplomatique, 1990, France, French |language=French |access-date=2026-03-12}}</ref>

In 2026, Koch-Miramond was announced as one of 72 historical women in STEM whose names have been proposed to be added to the [[List of the 72 names on the Eiffel Tower|72 men]] already celebrated on the [[Eiffel Tower]]. The plan was announced by the Mayor of Paris, [[Anne Hidalgo]] following the recommendations of a committee led by [[Isabelle Vauglin]] of [[Femmes et Sciences]] and Jean-François Martins, representing the operating company which runs the Eiffel Tower.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Eiffel Tower: a list of 72 women scientists will soon be inscribed on the Parisian monument |url=https://www.sortiraparis.com/en/news/in-paris/articles/340564-eiffel-tower-list-of-72-women-scientists-soon-to-be-honored-on-the-paris-landmark |access-date=2026-03-07 |website=www.sortiraparis.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=2026-01-26 |title=Eiffel Tower to honor 72 women scientists for posterity |url=https://www.lemonde.fr/en/france/article/2026/01/26/eiffel-tower-to-honor-72-women-in-science-for-posterity_6749828_7.html |access-date=2026-03-07 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Les noms des 72 femmes pour la Tour Eiffel ont été révélés. |url=https://www.femmesetsciences.fr/news/les-noms-des-72-femmes-pour-la-tour-eiffel-ont-%C3%A9t%C3%A9-r%C3%A9v%C3%A9l%C3%A9 |access-date=2026-03-07 |website=Femmes & Sciences |language=fr}}</ref><ref>[https://10ca8303-b3dc-4a91-9dcc-2d2b91792b47.usrfiles.com/ugd/10ca83_3838bd19a41a4e83927cfc8fe0f50404.pdf 72 femmes de sciences pour la tour Eiffel] ''Femmes & Sciences'' (in French). Retrieved 2026-03-07</ref>
